Clam ileocystoplasty in three steps: detubularize, reconfigure into a cup, and anastomose to the bivalved bladder
Yang-Monti channel construction: a short ileal segment is opened and re-rolled perpendicular to its axis over a catheter, so the bowel circumference becomes the new channel length
Hautmann W-configuration neobladder: detubularized ileum folded into a four-limb W, then closed into a low-pressure sphere with ureters at the top and urethra at the most dependent point
Bricker versus Wallace ureteroenteric anastomosis to an ileal conduit
Indiana pouch: a detubularized right-colon reservoir with ureters reimplanted, a tapered ileal efferent limb, and ileocecal-valve continence to a catheterizable stoma

Kock pouch: a detubularized ileal reservoir with an afferent antireflux nipple valve receiving the ureters and an efferent continence nipple valve leading to a catheterizable stoma, plus an inset of the one-way nipple-valve mechanism
Studer orthotopic neobladder: a detubularized ileal sphere anastomosed to the urethra at its most dependent point, with an intact afferent limb receiving the ureters
Anderson-Hynes dismembered pyeloplasty in three steps: obstructed UPJ, dismember and spatulate, dependent-funnel anastomosis
Transureteroureterostomy: the donor ureter crossed retroperitoneally above the aortic bifurcation to an end-to-side anastomosis with the healthy recipient ureter
Buccal mucosa graft ureteroplasty: non-transecting longitudinal ureterotomy, buccal onlay graft over a double-J stent, and an omental-wrap cross-section
Ileal ureter replacement: harvest an ileal segment and restore bowel continuity, then interpose it isoperistaltically between renal pelvis and bladder
Psoas hitch versus Boari flap: the psoas hitch fixes the bladder cephalad to bridge a short gap, while the Boari flap tubularizes a bladder-wall flap into a longer ureteral substitute
Three antireflux ureteral reimplantation techniques: Cohen cross-trigonal tunnel, Politano-Leadbetter new-hiatus tunnel, and Lich-Gregoir extravesical detrusorrhaphy

Sacrocolpopexy Y-mesh in sagittal view: anterior and posterior arms sutured to the vaginal walls join into a stem fixed to the anterior longitudinal ligament at the sacral promontory
Sacrospinous ligament fixation: the vaginal apex suspended to the sacrospinous ligament with sutures placed 1.5–2 cm medial to the ischial spine, clear of the pudendal bundle
Uterosacral ligament suspension: the vault suspended to the intermediate uterosacral ligaments toward the sacrum, with the ureter running 1-2 cm lateral and cystoscopy mandatory
Overlapping anal sphincteroplasty: the retracted external-sphincter ends are mobilized and overlapped vest-over-pants with mattress sutures
Transabdominal VVF repair, extravesical vs O'Conor: the extravesical approach leaves the bladder closed and dissects the vesicovaginal space from outside, the O'Conor bivalves the bladder
O'Conor transvesical VVF repair vs the extravesical approach: O'Conor bivalves the bladder sagittally down to the fistula; the extravesical approach leaves the bladder closed
Vesicovaginal fistula layered closure: a fistula tract repaired by tension-free multilayer closure with the bladder and vaginal suture lines offset, plus optional interposition
